summary.text: 水 is a pictograph of flowing water: a central current flanked by marks for droplets. Its basic and common meaning is “water.”

formation.text: The whole graph pictures flowing water. Oracle forms are described as a central stroke for the current and side dots for droplets; this is a whole-character pictorial analysis, not evidence for separate component characters. A Han-era account adds a cosmological interpretation, which is a historical explanation rather than the graph’s pictorial construction.

components.text: The whole character 水 is pictorial: the central stroke depicts a current and the side marks depict droplets. Oracle forms vary in the number of side marks; this account does not identify them as separate character components.

history.text: Oracle-script forms vary in their side marks. Bronze and Warring States forms are described as retaining the flowing-water picture. The selected oracle-script and Western Zhou bronze-script glyphs are modern vector redrawings, not photographs of artifacts; they illustrate forms but do not establish an evolutionary sequence.
A Han-era account glosses 水 as “level” and explains it through the cosmology of the time. This is a historical interpretation, distinct from the pictorial construction of the graph.

uncertainties.text: Proposals for the spoken word’s earlier pronunciation and possible connections to other languages differ and remain unresolved; they do not identify a phonetic component in 水.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone examples; individual dates unresolved
senses.text: Reported Shang oracle-bone examples use 水 for water or flooding. This is the earliest meaning supported in this dossier.
The common current meaning is “water.” Other recorded glosses include liquid, lotion, and juice; their chronology is not established here.

A bronze inscription is reported to use 水 for the different word 乞, “request.” This is graph borrowing: a written sign was reused because the words were proposed to sound alike or similarly, not because “water” developed into “request.” The sound match has not been independently established here.
One reported oracle-bone use has been read as a verb involving either leveling ground with water or washing a temple. Its reading and connection, if any, to the noun “water” remain unresolved.

developments.text: The graph was reportedly reused to write 乞, “request,” on the proposed basis that the words sounded alike or similarly. The dossier does not establish the pictured water’s old spoken name or a historical sound comparison between the two words.

limitations.text: The oracle-bone examples and their individual dates are not specified in detail here. The relationship between the disputed verbal use and the noun “water” is unresolved.
The proposed sound-based explanation for using 水 to write 乞 is not confirmed by a historical comparison of the two words’ pronunciations.

水準 is reported in a compound meaning “leveling instrument” and in an abstract sense meaning “standard” or “level.” Those compound meanings do not establish separate senses of 水, and their stages are undated here.

overview.text: 水 pictures flowing water, with a central current and marks for droplets. Its common meaning is “water.”

components.text: The central line and side marks together picture flowing water and droplets.
